title: Baltic Sea Region Youth Survey 2027: young people, tell us what matters to you
content:
The Baltic Sea Region Youth Forum (BSRYF) launches a region-wide survey on what matters to young people of age 16-30, and how much they trust politics. The survey is open until 14 December 2026.

How do young people in the Baltic Sea Region see their role in politics and society? The Baltic Sea Region Youth Forum (BSRYF), an independent body of young people supported by the Council of the Baltic Sea States (CBSS), has launched the Baltic Sea Region Youth Survey 2027 to find out.

The survey is open to young people in Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Poland and Sweden and available in all languages. It has four parts:

  • Regional relevance: how much eight topics matter to young people personally and for cooperation in the region, including climate protection, security and resilience, education and economic opportunities, migration, digital transformation, and infrastructure and mobility, and how much say they feel they have on each.
  • Trust in politics: whether young people feel represented, listened to and taken seriously by politicians.
  • Participation in practice: which forms of participation young people use, would consider, and can realistically access.

title: New Swedish Institute-funded projects contribute to the updated EUSBSR Action Plan
content:
From countering disinformation and strengthening democratic participation to advancing sustainable urban development, eighteen new projects funded by the Swedish Institute support the implementation of the updated EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region Action Plan.

The projects are funded through the Swedish Institute Baltic Sea and Eastern Partnership Programme and contribute to actions included in the draft revised Action Plan of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region. The projects bring together municipalities, universities, civil society organisations, public authorities and businesses to develop knowledge, strengthen capacities and build long-term partnerships across borders in line with the Strategy.

Several projects contribute to the Strategy’s increased focus on resilience, security and democratic participation.

title: AlgaeFood: When seaweed finds its way onto the plate
content:
Innovative local food production: Offer someone a piece of seaweed with a “Bon appetit!” and you are likely to be met with a degree of scepticism. Until they taste it, that is. More often than not, the next thing you hear is: “That actually tastes quite nice.”

The seaweed that grows along the Danish-German coast not only contributes to water quality, but can also be used as food – unfortunately, this happens all too rarely! Because seaweed is actually a ‘superfood’ and it is a regional resource with great potential. Depending on the species of algae, the seaweed contains protein, minerals and vitamins – and it grows in the sea without requiring agricultural land.

title: From first contact to lasting support: Baltic Sea Network explores youth outreach in Stockholm
content:
How can youth guidance centres reach young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET), particularly those who remain outside existing support systems? This question was at the centre of the Baltic Sea Network for Youth Guidance Centres and NEET Services meeting, held in Stockholm on 10–12 November 2026.

The City of Stockholm hosted the meeting as part of the School to Work flagship under Policy Area Education of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR). The event brought together youth guidance practitioners, employment specialists and policymakers to exchange experiences and explore approaches to reaching young people who may not actively seek assistance.

The Stockholm meeting built on the launch of the Baltic Sea Network for Youth Guidance Centres and NEET Services in Kraków, Poland, in March 2026. During that first gathering, participants identified outreach as a key challenge for youth guidance services, highlighting the importance of finding, engaging and motivating young people who are not reached through conventional support systems.

title: Taking catchment-based water management forward
content:
How can cooperation around catchment-based water management move from individual projects towards a more lasting Baltic Sea Region network?

This was the question at the heart of the Clean Water Alliances follow-up event on 11 November 2026. The online meeting continued the discussions started at the Clean Water Alliances event in Tallinn in May, bringing together catchment officers, projects, authorities and other experts to exchange experiences and consider practical next steps for cooperation across the Baltic Sea Region.

The follow-up was organised by EUSBSR Policy Areas Nutri and Hazards together with SIP LIFE WetEST, SIP LIFE ACWA and Interreg Central Baltic project BaltCOP. The programme combined practical experiences from catchment officers with discussion of the newly released BaltCOP Catchment Officer Guidebook, hazardous substances, funding and the future of pan-Baltic cooperation.

title: Share your views and help shape the future of PA Innovation
content:
As part of the review of Policy Area Innovation’s work during 2021–2026, organisations that have worked with PA Innovation are invited to share their experiences and perspectives through a questionnaire prepared by Policy Area Innovation.

A few minutes of your time to complete the questionnaire would be greatly appreciated. Your feedback will help assess the relevance and effectiveness of the actions and activities, reflect on collaboration with stakeholders, and identify areas for further development.

The questionnaire seeks your views on the work carried out so far and your suggestions for further developing activities and cooperation.

Share your views through the questionnaire:

https://forms.gle/3UNYK46Zi2oH1JNb7

We would be grateful if you could submit your responses by 25 November.

title: Age-friendly workplaces: experts assess 19 policy proposals
content:
How can we help people stay well and keep working as they grow older?

On 4 November 2026, the Solutions for Age-Friendly Employers (SAFE) project brought together nearly 50 experts from Estonia, Finland and Sweden to assess policy proposals for age-friendly working conditions. The online workshop examined two questions for each proposal: how much difference could it make, and how feasible would it be to put into practice?

The online workshop, Age-Friendly Workplaces: Ideas for Action, focused on how policy can help people aged 55+ stay in employment. The SAFE project focuses on health and social care, but the discussion showed that many of the questions apply across sectors. Can employees access training throughout their careers? Can they adjust their work when their needs change? And what support do managers need to make those changes possible?

title: Mental Health in All Policies: what the Baltic Sea Region can offer
content:
Policy Area Health Coordinator/Northern Dimension Partnership in Public Health and Social Well-being (NDPHS) Secretariat Director Ülla-Karin Nurm joined policymakers and experts to discuss the economic and social case for sustained investment in mental health at Mental Health Europe’s (MHE) conference “Investing in Mental Health for Resilient Societies”. Held at the Estonian Parliament (Riigikogu) in Tallinn on 4 November 2026, the conference brought together more than 130 participants in person and online, including researchers, civil society representatives and people with lived experience.

Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) modelling presented at the conference estimates that mental ill health costs around 1.7% of GDP across the EU, a figure comparable to the estimated costs of tobacco use or obesity. The conference also highlighted an access gap across OECD countries. Around 60% of people who need mental health care are unable to access it.

title: Interreg Baltic Sea Region programme continues the dialogue with the Strategy on future transnational cooperation
content:
This article is originally published on the Interreg Baltic Sea Region programme site, on 5 October 2026.

What should Interreg Baltic Sea Region, as a transnational cooperation programme, address after 2027? As work on the future Programme progresses, dialogue with regional stakeholders help further develop the cooperation needs identified by the Programme countries. The EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region is of particular importance in this process, bringing the macro-regional strategic perspective and helping to ensure that future cooperation needs are firmly rooted in the updated Action Plan and its implementation.

The Baltic Sea region is changing – and so are the challenges that cooperation needs to address. Security and resilience have gained urgency; climate impacts are becoming increasingly tangible; and demographic, green, and digital transitions are reshaping our territories and economies.

title: Four new Baltic Sea Region Cultural Pearls selected to strengthen social resilience in 2027
content:
The BSR Cultural Pearls Network is growing. Following a selection process that began in March, Gjøvik/Norway, Šilutė/Lithuania, Rēzekne/Latvia, and Hel/Poland have been selected as BSR Cultural Pearls 2027. These cities will continue their work towards strengthening social resilience through culture in their communities, starting from grassroot-level steps towards sustainable solutions.

Their selection emerged from a strong field of 13 candidates, demonstrating the interest among municipalities across the Baltic Sea Region in using culture to bring communities together and shape more resilient places.
